combined_coverage.limits: Full-file coverage is the union of explicitly attributed reviews. The coordinator independently reviewed only its listed 3,027 lines.

findings.behavior: Reads include subprocess-fixture assertions for native changelog marker persistence, preserving legacy and unrelated settings, and refusing stale-snapshot downgrade. These test bodies were inspected, not executed. Collapsed versus full content and current versus historical release selection are separately asserted.

findings.topic: Draft injection, key ownership, and auto-send
findings.behavior: Image-only queued messages retain images; path attachment retains a draft and pending-image restoration appends. The external monitor-DLL case is ignored and requires an explicit fixture environment; it proves no installed DLL availability. Stub callbacks test claimed press/release events, modal rejection of new claims, and forwarding an already-owned release. Pure auto-send decisions cover deadline, unchanged text, manual edit/clear/whitespace, and busy cancellation.

findings.topic: Editor change attribution and queue restoration
findings.behavior: Tests distinguish extension-injected editor changes from subsequent user edits and programmatic submit clear; the programmatic marker is consumed even without a subscriber. Helpers are checked for live-panel detection, merging queued and typed text, and setting a multiline UTF-8 caret using byte offsets.

The exact 15 wired menu rows are asserted; submenu rows have no cycle values and value rows include their current value. Tests cover live hide-thinking/images/cache notices, persisted padding/double-Escape/completion size, disabled or one-minute HTTP timeout, and ignored unknown keys. Trusted project settings merge per field with explicit false and zero retained; untrusted project fields are ignored; flat display keys take precedence over nested terminal fallback.

User bubbles, verbose-versus-quiet startup, resume command rendering, quoting and captured session-cwd trust are covered. Rendering helpers assert brand/capability lists and empty states. Resource reload tests replace context paths in both header and panel and remove stale data. Update notices cover failures, package-only updates, and empty reports. Fixture-generated subprocesses were not run.

Tests cover viewport overlap, ! versus !! parsing, bare bang fallback, cancellation without prematurely freeing the Bash run slot, and key press/repeat rather than release dispatch. Double-Escape and Ctrl-C helper windows include exactly 500 ms and exclude 501 ms. Windows paste tests synthesize burst timing and queued events, normalize CRLF, and ignore an Enter release in lookahead; they are not live Windows console integration.

Final assistant content updates the component and cached tail before detachment. Tab rendering and UTF-8 cursor helpers, slash suggestions, plain-text clearing, selection beyond five visible rows, ordinary draft arrow ownership, and @ paths after Chinese text are covered. The early Tab test manually reproduces replacement logic and its comment mentions a space while its assertion expects /model; later tests call accept_top_suggestion and check only starts_with, so neither is evidence of an exact trailing-space contract.

findings.topic: Command registry and synthetic event evidence limit
findings.behavior: Tests resolve canonical slash commands and aliases and assert a visible subset plus hidden entries. The test named test_agent_event_mapping_creates_assistant_and_tool explicitly manually applies message/tool mutations after saying a real terminal is unavailable; it does not invoke the event drain. It checks assistant text/thinking, tool registration and result removal, working-slot exclusion, retry display, editor-border loader and abort state.

Fresh args do not restore old history while continue/session args do. Aborted and errored assistant usage do not overwrite the last successful context badge. Selector tests round-trip one child and the selector flag. History skips consecutive duplicates and whitespace, browses without wrapping, and restores the user's prior draft.

Root continuation covers form serialization with literal environment references, duplicate detection, HTTP-scheme validation and configured-provider deletion. Test helper changes are isolated to temporary fixture directories. Provider switching checks matching default provider/model, configured protocol selection for duplicate model IDs, actual lane update before persistence, and preserving defaults on unknown/unavailable provider or closed-lane failure; selector status marks the live provider instead of the saved default. Adjacent function boundaries are owned by audit_extensions.

findings.topic: Diagnostics, model cycling, and configuration parsing
findings.behavior: Provider errors and aborts keep a useful diagnostic or fallback text. Sanitization removes terminal controls, normalizes CRLF, preserves tabs, caps long text with an ellipsis, and substitutes a blank-message fallback. Model-cycle helpers wrap, fall back for unknown IDs, and handle empty catalogs. Configured key parsing covers Ctrl+G and shift+tab.

Input/editor submit callbacks try-lock both dialog slots, establishing those helpers release locks before invoking callbacks. Prompt parsing covers flat and questions shapes, options/descriptions, multiple/freeform defaults, suggestions and confirm choices. Bridge tests correlate two queued requests, occupy one input slot at a time, answer/cancel by request ID, cancel queued work, and reject new requests after detach.
